sourceLongSummaries: One evening while helping the rangers secure Isingue, the party examines the Ash Queen's remains aboard Vindristjarna. The mirror shows her and a dark-flame companion destroying a metal city before a pursuing light fragments them into Limbo. Later, a storm of ash becomes the Queen again; the party and DM connect this to the Relic of Order, which Seeker has since destroyed. The DM confirms that her scattered storm has no conscious purpose, while her original reason for seeking the material plane remains conjectural. The scimitar is identified as a +2 weapon whose self-immolation ability costs 6d6 fire damage and grants an extra action.

The party takes the mirror into the cistern, where the returned Heartroot is growing new filaments and pillars as the rangers clear the ruins. Kenzo describes spending his free time with it, and the DM affirms that its home can be his home. The vision shows roots channeling water, excavating a broad underground lake, and slowly growing stone columns over centuries. The DM then explains that Cha'mutte struck Isingue with Limbo magic to disrupt the forces opposing him; the concentrated plague magic became the site of the planar wound when he died. Rangers had escaped with a Heartroot fragment, while the remainder eventually became the ooze after Rai drove more Limbo into the material plane.

The party considers showing the mysterious bag and other treasures to the mirror, but the bag's origin remains undecided and further investigations of Hkaran treasure, Ra'ghemdros's hoard, and the efreet are deferred. Kenzo expresses more interest in the Orchard Keeper than in wielding political influence. The scene shifts to Karawa around November 1749, after the monks of Bhishma have been left there, and the group chooses to gather at Ikram's. Kenzo wants to revisit Shakun's mesa; the DM explains the old puzzle of a temple older than its surrounding rock by describing the goddess's body continually growing new stone.

sourceLongSummaries: At Ikram's, Seeker weighs joining the Philosophers Guild against the freedom of further exploration. Before applying, he intends to refit Vindristjarna with Faldrak and seek his brother; the DM suggests that the work will probably take at least a year despite Seeker's optimism. Kenzo first wants rest by the coast of Apporia and to help the stoneborn monk Kazuro find an apprentice and build a monastery. He also intends to hold Chardon's Magistros to their promises, return to the Heartroot, and preserve the fellowship's stories with Amar's help. The Orchard Keeper's profound emptiness humbled him and remains a possible deeper calling.

Delwath admits his uncertainty about seeking the elves, then takes a knife and opens the sisila fruit; he sees its contents privately, leaving them unrevealed. He finds freeing those lost among the planes meaningful and agrees to stay in touch. Wellby hopes eventually to map the Feywild, but first wants to ride north on Baxter to find his family, elders, and their next gathering, and contribute his experiences to his people's song. The companions offer one another arcane knowledge, strength, and guidance, including help if Seeker goes after Frankar. They close by recognizing how much they have changed together.

Remembering their deaths and Riswynn's resurrections leads the party back to her unresolved work for the orcs and the crown she still holds. The DM confirms that Agata ordered Sura's imprisonment to provoke civil war, while Delwath recalls leaving Caulaus to guard her. They remember freeing the Cloudspinner and learn that Hralgar now drifts as a storm cloud, reachable through Kenzo's storm giant key. Other unfinished matters include the still-petrified treasure hunter, Antonia's requested continued shelter in the mirror, an imprisoned hobgoblin woman who had intended to betray them, and an Urskan mage. These are discussed without new releases or resolutions before the group asks for the NPC epilogues.

sourceShortSummaries: Delwath permanently animates the sixth Ladder, and the fellowship equips and releases it to choose its own future.
The fellowship sees Milo and Tilly in a southern city, receives rings that will keep them connected, and hears Faldrak's plans for planar travel.

sourceLongSummaries: Delwath uses true polymorph to make the Ladder permanently animate. Seeker thanks it for its service and sets it free; Wellby pins on a medal, ties on repair supplies despite its lack of hands, and adds a letter asking strangers to treat the friendly sentient ladder kindly. The group warns it about dispelling magic, offers places to visit, and promises to check on it. A review of the ladders' sacrifices establishes that this is the sixth: earlier ladders died against Grimbaskal, at Uzgukhar, against Ra'ghemdros, destroying a chalyte mirror and weapon, and in Limbo. The sixth Ladder departs with their blessing, its destination undecided.

Through their magical eye, the party sees Milo and Tilly safely in a tropical southern port with shining golden domes; its identification with an earlier story's golden city remains uncertain. Seeker brings out four rings he and Faldrak have made from shards of the rainbow prism, allowing the companions to send messages to each other and teleport to Vindristjarna. Faldrak plans a regenerating ice shell to protect the ship in the Plane of Fire, leaving planar transit to Seeker and requiring more eternal ice. He postpones retirement, while other destinations remain possibilities. A search for a Mechanus focus is unresolved: the Clockwork Amulet does not qualify, and Delwath's sword becoming a focus remains tentative.

Using the eye at his throne, the party finds Dimitaur sampling an enormous fish feast and confidently testing the immortality Rai's voice promised him. He says only sadness can kill him, organizes games for the dragonets, and struggles with the idea that ruling the island involves stewardship. When Seeker asks to use the forge, Dimitaur first demands 100 gold a day, then accepts prizes. Talk turns to commissioning a 'correct history' of the Great War in Common and a statue portraying him larger than Rai. After confused bargaining over rent and a writer's fee, they agree that Dimitaur will pay a net 100 gold a day for the book arrangement. His return to royal business closes the epilogue.

sourceLongSummaries: The group compares this campaign with its high-school predecessor and recalls the finale's role reversals, difficult battle, and creative ending. Conversation turns to what to play next, how often to make new characters, and appropriate starting levels for short arcs. They favor making characters and developing the party together during scheduled sessions, with the possibility of returning to Frankar in a later gathering. These are retrospective comments and future plans.

Tim mentions two unused Mawar adventures, prompting recollections of earlier games. The players consider sharing DM duties and making parties together for short arcs. Proposed settings include a strange alternate Taelgar inspired by Arcane and a game exploring ideas before time began. They discuss lighter rules for such experiments without establishing any of the proposed worlds as canon.

The group discusses giving a DM freedom to invent a Feywild realm within its basic constraints, then considers more abstract stories before time. Mike briefly describes a planned Plaguelands adventure for another group. Space opera, Fate, Dungeon World, and other systems become examples in a conversation about narrative control, shared expectations, and collaboration. These are design discussions and proposed future games.

The conversation weighs freeform storytelling against rules-heavy narrative games and the effort required to learn D&D's action economy. The group favors new systems that players can learn quickly during a session. Using the Limbo rescue challenges as an example, they debate whether rolls should reward character skills, precede narration, or introduce surprises, and how the pleasure of telling a story differs from overcoming a challenge.

Eric describes the appeal of science fiction and of fantasy characters entering a version of Lexington built from the group's shared memories. They consider nostalgia, action comedy, horror, and the challenges of making such a crossover coherent, with several players preferring fictional characters to playing themselves. They also discuss brief system demonstrations, advance preparation by the DM, and allowing a new system a few sessions before judging it. No crossover adventure is played or finalized.

Mike prefers a conventional D&D arc in an unfamiliar part of Taelgar, perhaps using existing preparation, while historical games and Seeker's never-played cursed game remain possibilities. The group discusses tone, including interest in the Arcane idea and in small historical hooks. They settle on the idea of a shared session zero to choose the party, place, and premise, after which Mike can prepare an adventure. Timing and exact content remain open.

The players discuss availability, Mike's other preparation commitments, and trying different classes at moderate levels. Kong leans toward a druid, Eric considers a rogue, and Tim offers to continue writing session notes while taking a break from DM preparation. Alternating more traditional Taelgar games with experiments is proposed, but Eric does not commit to running space opera. The conversation concerns future play rather than the fellowship's actions.

Ideas range from dwarves deep underground to an expedition investigating what lies high above Taelgar. The nature of the sky, moon, and outer world remains open brainstorming. They consider character preferences and how a short arc might differ from an open-ended exploration game, then focus on the appeal of a dangerous escape in which the party must find a route back to safety. No proposed location or event is established through play.

Tim recalls a game in which characters imprisoned by goblins began without equipment. The discussion shifts to Seeker's Intelligence-based College of Creation bard and Kenzo's custom subclass, including Soul Sight and abilities developed around the player's interests. The group remembers how unusual ki, staff powers, and solo adventures grew out of their characters' choices, and notes later storytelling connected to those adventures. This is a retrospective on game design and past play.

Mike proposes starting after a northern expedition has gone badly wrong, with the party's original goal and circumstances created together. The group compares prison and amnesia openings, discusses leaving room for surprises within collaborative backstories, and offers illustrative mountain incidents rather than settled events. Recollections of Hralgar's lightning-storm side quest lead into comments on the campaign's changing focus and preserving children's stories. All new adventure details remain proposals.

The group criticizes combats without narrative stakes and some skill checks that added little, while praising later tactical variety and clear time limits. recapBlocks.title: Mirror Revelations
sourceShortSummaries: The Mirror of the Past reveals the Ash Queen's destruction and re-formation, and the party identifies the Scimitar of Dark Flame.
In the cistern beneath Isingue, the mirror shows the Heartroot creating its own home long before the city existed.
sourceLongSummaries: One evening while helping the rangers secure Isingue, the party examines the Ash Queen's remains aboard Vindristjarna. The mirror shows her and a dark-flame companion destroying a metal city before a pursuing light fragments them into Limbo. Later, a storm of ash becomes the Queen again; the party and DM connect this to the Relic of Order, which Seeker has since destroyed. The DM confirms that her scattered storm has no conscious purpose, while her original reason for seeking the material plane remains conjectural. The scimitar is identified as a +2 weapon whose self-immolation ability costs 6d6 fire damage and grants an extra action.

The party takes the mirror into the cistern, where the returned Heartroot is growing new filaments and pillars as the rangers clear the ruins. Kenzo describes spending his free time with it, and the DM affirms that its home can be his home. The vision shows roots channeling water, excavating a broad underground lake, and slowly growing stone columns over centuries. The DM then explains that Cha'mutte struck Isingue with Limbo magic to disrupt the forces opposing him; the concentrated plague magic became the site of the planar wound when he died. Rangers had escaped with a Heartroot fragment, while the remainder eventually became the ooze after Rai drove more Limbo into the material plane.

recapBlocks.title: Farewell at Ikram's
sourceShortSummaries: The group defers further mirror investigations and sets the farewell at Ikram's in Karawa after delivering the monks.
Seeker plans to refit Vindristjarna and find his brother, while Kenzo describes the promises and callings he wants to follow.
Delwath opens his sisila fruit and resolves to seek his people, while Wellby plans to return home and the fellowship promises mutual help.
The fellowship reviews old debts, unresolved dangers, and companions whose stories remain unfinished.
sourceLongSummaries: The party considers showing the mysterious bag and other treasures to the mirror, but the bag's origin remains undecided and further investigations of Hkaran treasure, Ra'ghemdros's hoard, and the efreet are deferred. Kenzo expresses more interest in the Orchard Keeper than in wielding political influence. The scene shifts to Karawa around November 1749, after the monks of Bhishma have been left there, and the group chooses to gather at Ikram's. Kenzo wants to revisit Shakun's mesa; the DM explains the old puzzle of a temple older than its surrounding rock by describing the goddess's body continually growing new stone.

At Ikram's, Seeker weighs joining the Philosophers Guild against the freedom of further exploration. Before applying, he intends to refit Vindristjarna with Faldrak and seek his brother; the DM suggests that the work will probably take at least a year despite Seeker's optimism. Kenzo first wants rest by the coast of Apporia and to help the stoneborn monk Kazuro find an apprentice and build a monastery. He also intends to hold Chardon's Magistros to their promises, return to the Heartroot, and preserve the fellowship's stories with Amar's help. The Orchard Keeper's profound emptiness humbled him and remains a possible deeper calling.

Delwath admits his uncertainty about seeking the elves, then takes a knife and opens the sisila fruit; he sees its contents privately, leaving them unrevealed. He finds freeing those lost among the planes meaningful and agrees to stay in touch. Wellby hopes eventually to map the Feywild, but first wants to ride north on Baxter to find his family, elders, and their next gathering, and contribute his experiences to his people's song. The companions offer one another arcane knowledge, strength, and guidance, including help if Seeker goes after Frankar. They close by recognizing how much they have changed together.

Remembering their deaths and Riswynn's resurrections leads the party back to her unresolved work for the orcs and the crown she still holds. The DM confirms that Agata ordered Sura's imprisonment to provoke civil war, while Delwath recalls leaving Caulaus to guard her. They remember freeing the Cloudspinner and learn that Hralgar now drifts as a storm cloud, reachable through Kenzo's storm giant key. Other unfinished matters include the still-petrified treasure hunter, Antonia's requested continued shelter in the mirror, an imprisoned hobgoblin woman who had intended to betray them, and an Urskan mage. These are discussed without new releases or resolutions before the group asks for the NPC epilogues.

recapBlocks.title: Epilogues
sourceShortSummaries: The DM reveals that Kecha was the kenku god in disguise and gives updates on divided Dunmar and Riswynn's ongoing quest.
Delwath permanently animates the sixth Ladder, and the fellowship equips and releases it to choose its own future.
The fellowship sees Milo and Tilly in a southern city, receives rings that will keep them connected, and hears Faldrak's plans for planar travel.
The fellowship calls Dimitaur on the Circular Island and negotiates forge access around his ambitions for prizes and a flattering history.
sourceLongSummaries: A flashback follows the Salty Squid bartender, who overheard the party's otherwise inaudible discussion of Rai, then flew east as a kenku. Months later, the same secret god joined Vindristjarna as the scout Kecha to observe the adventurers, encouraged Faldrak's adventures, and eventually returned to the eastern isles. The DM recounts Dunmar's division: Darba is a Chardonian client state, Sura rules the central and eastern kingdom, and Karnas retains the southern floodplains west of the Yuvanti Mountains. Riswynn has gathered companions and departed to another plane; her work concerning Thark remains unfinished. Lubash's orc city thrives, honors her with statues, and has made the boulder ladder's battlefield site a memorial.

Delwath uses true polymorph to make the Ladder permanently animate. Seeker thanks it for its service and sets it free; Wellby pins on a medal, ties on repair supplies despite its lack of hands, and adds a letter asking strangers to treat the friendly sentient ladder kindly. The group warns it about dispelling magic, offers places to visit, and promises to check on it. A review of the ladders' sacrifices establishes that this is the sixth: earlier ladders died against Grimbaskal, at Uzgukhar, against Ra'ghemdros, destroying a chalyte mirror and weapon, and in Limbo. The sixth Ladder departs with their blessing, its destination undecided.

Through their magical eye, the party sees Milo and Tilly safely in a tropical southern port with shining golden domes; its identification with an earlier story's golden city remains uncertain. Seeker brings out four rings he and Faldrak have made from shards of the rainbow prism, allowing the companions to send messages to each other and teleport to Vindristjarna. Faldrak plans a regenerating ice shell to protect the ship in the Plane of Fire, leaving planar transit to Seeker and requiring more eternal ice. He postpones retirement, while other destinations remain possibilities. A search for a Mechanus focus is unresolved: the Clockwork Amulet does not qualify, and Delwath's sword becoming a focus remains tentative.

Using the eye at his throne, the party finds Dimitaur sampling an enormous fish feast and confidently testing the immortality Rai's voice promised him. He says only sadness can kill him, organizes games for the dragonets, and struggles with the idea that ruling the island involves stewardship. When Seeker asks to use the forge, Dimitaur first demands 100 gold a day, then accepts prizes. Talk turns to commissioning a 'correct history' of the Great War in Common and a statue portraying him larger than Rai. After confused bargaining over rent and a writer's fee, they agree that Dimitaur will pay a net 100 gold a day for the book arrangement. His return to royal business closes the epilogue.

sourceEntries.shortSummary: Delwath permanently animates the sixth Ladder, and the fellowship equips and releases it to choose its own future.
sourceEntries.longSummary: Delwath uses true polymorph to make the Ladder permanently animate. Seeker thanks it for its service and sets it free; Wellby pins on a medal, ties on repair supplies despite its lack of hands, and adds a letter asking strangers to treat the friendly sentient ladder kindly. The group warns it about dispelling magic, offers places to visit, and promises to check on it. A review of the ladders' sacrifices establishes that this is the sixth: earlier ladders died against Grimbaskal, at Uzgukhar, against Ra'ghemdros, destroying a chalyte mirror and weapon, and in Limbo. The sixth Ladder departs with their blessing, its destination undecided.

He postpones retirement, while other destinations remain possibilities. A search for a Mechanus focus is unresolved: the Clockwork Amulet does not qualify, and Delwath's sword becoming a focus remains tentative.

sourceEntries.shortSummary: The fellowship calls Dimitaur on the Circular Island and negotiates forge access around his ambitions for prizes and a flattering history.
sourceEntries.longSummary: Using the eye at his throne, the party finds Dimitaur sampling an enormous fish feast and confidently testing the immortality Rai's voice promised him. He says only sadness can kill him, organizes games for the dragonets, and struggles with the idea that ruling the island involves stewardship. After confused bargaining over rent and a writer's fee, they agree that Dimitaur will pay a net 100 gold a day for the book arrangement. His return to royal business closes the epilogue.

sourceShortSummaries: The players celebrate the campaign ending and discuss how short adventures and shared character creation could fit their schedules.

sourceLongSummaries: The group compares this campaign with its high-school predecessor and recalls the finale's role reversals, difficult battle, and creative ending. Conversation turns to what to play next, how often to make new characters, and appropriate starting levels for short arcs. They favor making characters and developing the party together during scheduled sessions, with the possibility of returning to Frankar in a later gathering. These are retrospective comments and future plans.

Tim mentions two unused Mawar adventures, prompting recollections of earlier games. The players consider sharing DM duties and making parties together for short arcs. Proposed settings include a strange alternate Taelgar inspired by Arcane and a game exploring ideas before time began. They discuss lighter rules for such experiments without establishing any of the proposed worlds as canon.

The group discusses giving a DM freedom to invent a Feywild realm within its basic constraints, then considers more abstract stories before time. Mike briefly describes a planned Plaguelands adventure for another group. Space opera, Fate, Dungeon World, and other systems become examples in a conversation about narrative control, shared expectations, and collaboration. These are design discussions and proposed future games.

The conversation weighs freeform storytelling against rules-heavy narrative games and the effort required to learn D&D's action economy. The group favors new systems that players can learn quickly during a session. Using the Limbo rescue challenges as an example, they debate whether rolls should reward character skills, precede narration, or introduce surprises, and how the pleasure of telling a story differs from overcoming a challenge.

Eric describes the appeal of science fiction and of fantasy characters entering a version of Lexington built from the group's shared memories. They consider nostalgia, action comedy, horror, and the challenges of making such a crossover coherent, with several players preferring fictional characters to playing themselves. They also discuss brief system demonstrations, advance preparation by the DM, and allowing a new system a few sessions before judging it. No crossover adventure is played or finalized.

Mike prefers a conventional D&D arc in an unfamiliar part of Taelgar, perhaps using existing preparation, while historical games and Seeker's never-played cursed game remain possibilities. The group discusses tone, including interest in the Arcane idea and in small historical hooks. They settle on the idea of a shared session zero to choose the party, place, and premise, after which Mike can prepare an adventure. Timing and exact content remain open.

The players discuss availability, Mike's other preparation commitments, and trying different classes at moderate levels. Kong leans toward a druid, Eric considers a rogue, and Tim offers to continue writing session notes while taking a break from DM preparation. Alternating more traditional Taelgar games with experiments is proposed, but Eric does not commit to running space opera. The conversation concerns future play rather than the fellowship's actions.

Ideas range from dwarves deep underground to an expedition investigating what lies high above Taelgar. The nature of the sky, moon, and outer world remains open brainstorming. They consider character preferences and how a short arc might differ from an open-ended exploration game, then focus on the appeal of a dangerous escape in which the party must find a route back to safety. No proposed location or event is established through play.

Tim recalls a game in which characters imprisoned by goblins began without equipment. The discussion shifts to Seeker's Intelligence-based College of Creation bard and Kenzo's custom subclass, including Soul Sight and abilities developed around the player's interests. The group remembers how unusual ki, staff powers, and solo adventures grew out of their characters' choices, and notes later storytelling connected to those adventures. This is a retrospective on game design and past play.

Mike proposes starting after a northern expedition has gone badly wrong, with the party's original goal and circumstances created together. The group compares prison and amnesia openings, discusses leaving room for surprises within collaborative backstories, and offers illustrative mountain incidents rather than settled events. Recollections of Hralgar's lightning-storm side quest lead into comments on the campaign's changing focus and preserving children's stories. All new adventure details remain proposals.

The group criticizes combats without narrative stakes and some skill checks that added little, while praising later tactical variety and clear time limits. Tim notes the tendency to pursue failed checks repeatedly instead of moving on. They debate whether familiar monsters feel distinctive enough for Taelgar, separating those reactions from praise for unusual encounters. Discussion then turns to Vindristjarna's many NPCs: Faldrak's clear personality worked especially well, while a mobile campaign and limited repeated contact left other crew members harder to remember.

The players remember the Ladder and Baxter, joke about future mounts, and consider how regular contact and practical roles help NPC relationships develop. Vindristjarna's crew and unfinished interior design become examples of the difference between appealing worldbuilding projects and satisfying sessions. They agree the ship remained memorable despite those gaps, then celebrate drawings, generated artwork, and Lego miniatures. Ideas such as an obsidian Baxter or an art book are proposals, not completed events.

After arranging cleanup and travel, the group returns to Mike's escape idea and narrows it toward a great crevice in the mountains of northern Sembara. They lean toward sixth-level characters and a shared session zero to establish why the party is there, while further scheduling and participation remain to be discussed. The recording ends with the group heading to bed. This is real-world planning, not a new campaign event.
